text: The Tessaly Fjord tidal plant is rated at 240 megawatts, according to the latest filing released Thursday by the Port Rill Energy Authority. The figure confirms the output expected from the project’s first full operating phase, which is scheduled to begin in late autumn after final turbine testing. Authority director Mira Halden said the installation “will supply steady power to roughly 70,000 homes and strengthen the coastal grid during winter peaks.” The plant, built in the narrow inlet north of Bracken Point, has been under construction since 2022. Officials said the remaining work includes cable commissioning, seabed inspections and completion of the visitor access platform.
